title: Operating Instructions
subtitle: Outpost Tucunaré — Relief Operator Sheet
preamble: Read before the first watch. Fold this sheet when finished. HQ expects business as usual.

sections.heading: 1. Power the set
steps: Turn the Power dial to ON. The lamp should glow yellow.
If the lamp is dark, check batteries before calling for a generator run.
Power OFF when you leave the chair — the set draws hard overnight.

sections.heading: 2. Tune the channel
steps: Set Band (1–5) and Meter (A–B–C) as posted for the night’s sched.
Turn the main Tune dial (or drag) until the frequency display matches the call.
Soft static under the channel is normal. A sharp blip means traffic may be present.

sections.heading: 3. Log incoming messages
steps: Open the field notes drawer. Every reply you choose is written into the book.
Copy sender, frequency, and substance. Margin notes are allowed; invent nothing for HQ.
Thoughts and journal scraps also go in the notes — keep them separate from net traffic.

sections.heading: 4. Relay, bury, or static
steps: When choices appear: Relay sends the content on; Bury logs privately; Static claims you did not copy.
Relay costs batteries and may change who trusts you. Bury protects some voices. Static is silence with a cost of its own.
Assistance requests (medical, route, window) follow the same three paths — choose before the meter falls.

sections.heading: 5. Maintain power & supplies
steps: Watch the battery gauge. Relays and boat surveys both spend charge.
Food, batteries, and medicine drain each night you sleep. Do not run any to zero.
If supplies fail, the outpost goes dark. Conserve on quiet nights; spend when a life is on the line.

sections.heading: 6. Desk tools
steps: Map: survey coordinate squares; send the boat only when you can spare batteries.
Sched Log: 24-hour listen windows and assigned frequencies. Prefer typed blocks over margin ink.
This sheet: fold it back when done. Do not relay its contents on the open net.

footer: — Desk copy. Prior operator’s handwriting in the margin is not procedure.
